title: Hedged streaming + bulk embeddings ingest with idempotent async job lifecycle
creator: Marco Chen
description:
Problem: Large customers are hitting two failure modes when importing millions of documents for embeddings + reranking: (1) synchronous per-request timeouts or head-of-line latency spikes when a single huge import blocks the inference queue, and (2) duplicate documents or partial commits after retries or network failures. We also need better observability and deterministic cost accounting for large imports.

Proposal summary: Implement a hedged streaming + bulk ingest surface that supports three ingestion modes: a) small synchronous batch API for up to N documents, b) streaming chunk uploads for mid-size imports (HTTP/2 or gRPC streaming with NDJSON chunks and resumable offsets), and c) long-running async job API for very large imports (multipart upload or pointer-to-cloud-storage). Core capabilities: server-side micro-batching for high GPU throughput, idempotency-key-based deduplication and exactly-once commit semantics, job lifecycle endpoints (create/status/cancel/list), hedged requests to alternative pools when queues stall, and configurable commit window/TTL for dedupe entries.

API sketch:
- POST /v1/embeddings:batch  -- sync, accepts up to 5k items, immediate response with embedding ids and failures.
- POST /v1/embeddings:jobs  -- starts an async job, returns job_id and upload_url for large file or supports chunked streaming session.
- POST /v1/embeddings:stream?sess={id}  -- streaming chunks (ndjson) with finalization marker; supports resume via offsets.
- GET /v1/embeddings:jobs/{job_id}  -- job status (queued/running/completed/failed), progress metrics, per-shard error samples.
- Header: X-Redwood-Idempotency-Key (client-supplied), optional client-side dedupe-hash per item.

Server semantics:
- Idempotency table keyed by (idempotency_key, client_project_id) with 48h TTL by default.
- Each streaming session writes a session checkpoint (last-acknowledged offset) so retries resume safely.
- Micro-batching: runtime groups items into 32-512 item micro-batches tuned per model and runtime. Batches are hedged: if a batch sits queued > hedging_threshold_ms, the system optionally dispatches the batch to a secondary compatible pool to reduce p50/p99 latency.
- Commit model: inference results are buffered and committed to the persistent index in atomic per-commit units. If a job is retried, already-applied commit ids are skipped using the idempotency ledger.
- Failure model: transient errors -> automatic retry at runtime with exponential backoff and jitter; permanent per-item errors recorded to job error table and surfaced in job results.

Operational telemetry & observability: emit metrics and traces for job_enqueue_latency, microbatch_latency, hedged_dispatch_count, dedupe_hits, commit_latency_p50/p95/p99, job_failures_by_reason. Add per-job timeline visible in Console with token-level cost estimate and a preview sample of canonical embeddings for QA.

Storage/consistency considerations: dedupe ledger needs compacting; implement a TTL background compactor. For multi-tenant scale we shard idempotency ledger by project_id and use a small LRU cache in front to reduce RPS on the ledger for hot uploads.

Rollout plan: implement server-side API in a feature-flagged manner; internal canary for low-volume customers, then progressive rollout to dedicated capacity and hosted accounts. Expose an opt-in flag in Console and API v2 header for customers who want deterministic exactly-once ingestion.

Why different from existing work: this ticket focuses on combining streaming resume semantics, hedged micro-batching for latency-sensitive workloads, and strict idempotency/commit ledger semantics into a single job lifecycle. It intentionally separates from prior bulk import tickets by adding hedging, job checkpoints, and a dedicated dedupe ledger design for large-scale parallel imports.
acceptance_criteria: New APIs implemented: /v1/embeddings:jobs, /v1/embeddings:stream, /v1/embeddings:batch documented in OpenAPI and SDKs
Idempotency: X-Redwood-Idempotency-Key prevents duplicate commits for retried requests within the TTL window (integration test coverage)
Streaming resume: client can resume a stream after network interruption using session id and offset; end-to-end test with interrupted upload passes and results identical to uninterrupted run
Hedged micro-batching reduces observed p99 embed latency for large imports by at least 30% in the canary cluster compared to baseline without hedging (metric verified)
Async job lifecycle: create/status/cancel endpoints implemented + job retention policy + console UI for per-job timeline
Per-job cost estimate and sample output preview appear in Console for canary customers
Monitoring: dashboards added for microbatch_latency, dedupe_hits, hedged_dispatch_count, job_failures_by_reason and alerts for job_fail_rate > 1% over 10m
Migration: existing import clients continue to work unchanged; SDKs include new helpers and clear migration docs
Performance: system sustains 5x current single-cluster ingestion throughput for 1M+ doc jobs in perf harness
Security: idempotency keys and job metadata do not leak across projects; verified by automated integration test
